# GEMS

[Global Examination of Mental State]{.sub}
:::

::: {.chips}
[<i class="bi bi-clipboard2-pulse"></i> In person, paper and pencil]{.chip}
[<i class="bi bi-clock"></i> About 10 minutes]{.chip}
[<i class="bi bi-list-check"></i> 11 tasks]{.chip}
[<i class="bi bi-files"></i> Parallel forms A and B]{.chip}
[<i class="bi bi-people"></i> 635 adults, 18–100 years]{.chip}
:::

::: {.prose}
GEMS is a brief paper-and-pencil screening for global cognition. It is not tied to a specific diagnosis and can be used for impairments of any origin.
Its 11 tasks cover **orientation, memory, working memory, visuo-spatial, visuo-constructional and planning abilities, perceptual and visual attention, language** (naming, comprehension and verbal fluency) and **pragmatics**.
The total score ranges from 0 to 100. Every task contributes with equal weight, and there is no ceiling effect in healthy adults.

Cut-offs are computed for age, sex, education and the **Cognitive Reserve Index**, which makes the comparison with peers more precise.
The parallel forms (GEMS-A and GEMS-B) and the thresholds for significant change support follow-up assessments.
:::
